newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's ACES airline to sell off 30 pct stake.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's ACES airline to sell off 30 pct stake.

text.p: Colombia's second largest airline Aerolineas Centrales de Colombia (ACES) is to sell a 30 percent stake in its operations, company chairman Juan Emilio Posada said Tuesday.
The decision is part of a wider strategy to modernize and expand the airline, which flies domestic and international routes.
Exisiting shareholders will inject about $10 million into the company before selling the stake and floating the airline on the stock exchange, Posada told reporters.
"This process reflects our intention to prepare the company for a stock floatation," Posada said.

The company is already in the process of overhauling its fleet and has placed orders for eight Airbus Industrie A320 aircraft which will be introduced in pairs starting November to replace the Boeing B-727s that it currently uses.

Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation and regional coffee growers' associations have a 54 percent holding in ACES. Merchant shipping line Flota Mercante Grancolombiana, which in turn is majority-owned by the National Coffee Growers' Federation, has a 44 percent stake in the airline.
